channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Ministries enhance security measures for new academic year
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Interior and Education Ministries are increasing security measures as the 2026-2027 academic year begins on September 15. Law enforcement will focus on public order and student safety around schools, monitoring traffic rules, and conducting preventive work. Drivers are urged to exercise caution near schools, and parents are asked to discuss road safety with their children.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Lawyer seeks help to compensate victim in nephrologist's case
item.description: The lawyer for convicted Kyrgyz nephrologist Nasira Beishebaeva is seeking public assistance to help her compensate a patient. The Bishkek City Court sentenced Beishebaeva to three years in prison and ordered her to pay over 2 million soms in damages. Her lawyer stated the sum is unaffordable for the doctor and appealed for donations.

item.title: Gas Supply Temporarily Suspended in Parts of Bishkek
item.description: Gas supplies will be temporarily suspended from September 14-16 in specific areas of Bishkek due to gas pipeline reconnection. Bishkekgaz apologizes for the inconvenience and advises consumers to use alternative energy sources during the outage.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Building "New Silk Road" with South Korea
item.description: In an article published in South Korea's The Chosun Daily, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed establishing a "New Silk Road" for the 21st century. He analyzed historical ties, strategic partnership, and future priorities, emphasizing advanced manufacturing and transport corridors.

item.title: ABank receives top rating from independent Sustainable Fitch for green financing program
item.description: ABank has received an 'Excellent' rating from Sustainable Fitch for its Green Financing Program, developed in partnership with the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI). This independent assessment confirms the program's high alignment with international capital market principles and sustainable finance standards, paving the way for ABank's entry into the international green bond market.

item.title: Uzbekistan sees increase in court cases of violence against women
item.description: Uzbek courts reviewed 2,018 criminal cases related to violence and harassment against women in the first half of 2026. This represents a 65.7% increase from the same period in 2025. Over 2,480 individuals were involved, with 1,624 convicted.

item.title: Saudi oil exports at risk as global supply could drop by 4%
item.description: Saudi oil exports face risks, with potential for a 4% drop in global supply, according to Reuters. The Tadawul All Share Index (TASI) fell 1.3% on September 13, marking its largest daily decline since early April.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host International Forum on Sustainable Tourism Development
item.description: Dushanbe will host the "Dushanbe International Tourism Exhibition – 2026" and the International Forum "City Integration in Realizing Sustainable Tourism Opportunities" from September 24-26. An organizing committee has been formed to manage these events, which aim to boost sustainable tourism, intercity cooperation, investment, and Tajikistan's tourism potential.

item.title: UK Ambassador to Uzbekistan Concludes Mission, Discusses Reforms and Regional Security
item.description: Concluding his mission in Tashkent, UK Ambassador Timothy Smart reflected on strengthening bilateral relations in trade, investment, education, and security. He emphasized Uzbekistan's independence and territorial integrity's importance to the UK and highlighted regional cooperation prospects, noting significant changes in the region since 2016.

item.title: Farg'ona Court Sentences 20-Year-Old and Accomplice for Grandmother's Murder and Arson
item.description: A 20-year-old man and his accomplice have been sentenced in Farg'ona for murdering his grandmother and setting her apartment on fire. The court found the first defendant guilty of murder, theft, and intentional property damage, sentencing him to 17 years imprisonment.

item.title: Russian Strike Hits Train Traveling from Ukraine to Poland; Boris Johnson's Train Also at Risk
item.description: A train traveling from Ukraine to Poland was struck by a Russian attack near Warsaw, endangering European diplomats. Polish Prime Minister warned of escalating conflict. The locomotive of the passenger train was hit by a drone attack.

item.title: Water Supply Interruption in Bishkek Affects Three Residential Areas and City Parts
item.description: Bishkekvodokanal announced a drinking water supply suspension in parts of Bishkek on September 16, from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. The outage will impact specific streets and the Altyn Ordo, Kara-Zhygach, and Politseysky Gorodok residential areas due to maintenance at the Kontrrezervuary water intake facility.

item.title: BRICS Summit: Putin, Xi Jinping, and Modi Advocate for a New World Order
item.description: Leaders of Russia, China, and India are pushing for a new world order, according to BBC reporting on the BRICS summit in New Delhi. Indian Prime Minister Modi stated that BRICS nations should increasingly shape global rules rather than follow them, emphasizing the role of the Global South and advocating for UN Security Council reform.

item.title: Kazakh Tenge Reaches Yearly Highs, Russian Ruble Also Rises: Currency Rates for September 14
item.description: The Russian ruble and Kazakh tenge have reached monthly and yearly highs, respectively. The euro and Chinese yuan have slightly decreased in value, while the US dollar's exchange rate remained unchanged. These figures are based on data from the National Bank of Kyrgyzstan and Bishkek exchange offices.

item.title: German companies in Uzbekistan paid 5.1 trillion soms in taxes over eight months
item.description: German companies operating in Uzbekistan paid 5.1 trillion soms in taxes during the first eight months of the year. The Tax Committee reported this figure is an 8% increase compared to the previous year. Approximately 300 German companies currently employ 46,600 people in the republic.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's employment center updates status of several foreign work agencies
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Interdepartmental Commission for Employment Abroad reviewed five agencies sending citizens to Serbia, Germany, Poland, and Russia. 'Human Capital' received a one-year permit for Serbia under undisclosed conditions. 'Tugese Recruitment' also had its permit extended for Germany. 'Globus Key KG Plus' for Russia retained its permit.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Launch Cross-Border QR Payments with Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to introduce cross-border QR payments with Kyrgyzstan, according to Bynur Zhalenov, Deputy Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan. This initiative, part of a phased rollout expected by summer 2027, will allow citizens to pay for goods and services using their existing banking apps and QR codes in 11 countries. The system is anticipated to be operational with China by year-end.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Reports 34% Increase in Bank Deposits Over One Year
item.description: Bank deposits in Uzbekistan have increased by 34% in one year, according to the Central Bank. The regulator stated that this significant growth contributes to the expansion of financial resources, with the largest portion deposited for terms up to one year.

item.title: Uzbek President Emphasizes Unity and Reforms Amid Global Risks
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stressed the importance of national unity, peace, and accelerating reforms in Tashkent. He highlighted the need to understand national identity and the value of labor and citizen satisfaction with reforms. He also linked internal reforms to seeking international partners.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Silk Road Fund to Finance Infrastructure Projects with $395 Million
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Bank for Foreign Economic Activity and the Silk Road Fund signed an agreement to finance infrastructure projects in Uzbekistan for up to $395 million. The deal was reached during the 11th "Belt and Road" Summit in Hong Kong. The focus will be on modernizing transport infrastructure, including toll roads.

item.title: Uzbekistan imported least gasoline in August since start of year
item.description: Uzbekistan imported the least amount of gasoline in August compared to any month since the beginning of the year. Fuel imports in August were 7.8 times lower than in January. The cost of imported gasoline has significantly increased.

item.title: Russia Targets Truck Near NATO and Poland Border
item.description: Russia targeted a truck near the NATO and Poland border, approximately 800 meters from the Dorohusk–Yahodin crossing point. Moscow stated the strike was aimed at infrastructure used for transporting military cargo from Europe to Ukraine.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Cover Part of Business Loan Interest Rates
item.description: Uzbekistan will cover a portion of bank loan interest rates for entrepreneurs. The compensation will not consider credit history, business category, or stability rating. Interest-free lending for family entrepreneurship will increase.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Forge Special Strategic Partnership in Technology and Industry
item.description: Uzbekistan designates South Korea as a key partner for technological and industrial cooperation, elevating relations to a special strategic partnership. This move aligns with Uzbekistan's pragmatic foreign policy and aims to transform its geographic advantage into technological capital amidst global competition in advanced manufacturing.

item.title: Power outages scheduled in Bishkek and regions of Kyrgyzstan on September 14
item.description: Intermittent power supply is expected in Bishkek and various regions of Kyrgyzstan on September 14 due to scheduled maintenance. Specific addresses and timeframes for the outages in the capital and surrounding areas have been announced by the electricity network enterprises.

item.title: Medvedev threatens to erase Lithuania from world map over nuclear weapons deployment
item.description: Dmitry Medvedev threatened to erase Lithuania from the world map, warning Vilnius of consequences for deploying nuclear weapons on its territory. He stated that NATO's Article 5 would not be practically applied against Russia.

item.title: BRICS Summit in New Delhi Focuses on Future Cooperation Amid Global Changes
item.description: The 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi is a platform for defining future cooperation and discussing international and regional agendas amidst global economic and security shifts. Chinese President Xi Jinping highlighted 20 years of BRICS cooperation, emphasizing peace, stability, innovation, and mutual understanding.

item.title: Experts urge Central Asia to enhance cybersecurity through data sharing and financial literacy
item.description: Experts recommend Central Asian countries prioritize continuous data exchange and improve citizens' financial literacy in cybersecurity. They advise abandoning outdated approaches for modern realities in developing protection mechanisms. This was discussed at the Silk Road Finance & Technology Forum in Tashkent.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Criminal Liability for Interfering with Judicial Proceedings
item.description: Uzbekistan's Criminal Code now penalizes officials who illegally influence judges to obstruct fair trials, issue unjust rulings, or secure specific decisions. Those found guilty face up to five years in prison.

item.title: Karalpakstan Officials Meet with German Cooperation Society (GIZ) Representatives
item.description: Officials from the Republic of Karalpakstan met with representatives from the German Society for International Cooperation (GIZ). Discussions focused on close partnership between Germany and Uzbekistan, reforms in Aral Sea region development, and joint projects in economy, ecology, medicine, and education.

item.title: Xi Jinping Calls for Expanded BRICS Cooperation and Global South Collaboration
item.description: At the BRICS summit in New Delhi, Chinese President Xi Jinping urged for enhanced cooperation and interaction among member states. He emphasized the growing importance of the Global South in shaping a multipolar world and proposed five initiatives for cooperation in AI, trade, digital economy, manufacturing, and human resources.

item.title: BRICS Summit in New Delhi: India and China's Role in a Transforming Multipolar World
item.description: The BRICS Summit in New Delhi is a significant moment for evolving a multipolar international order. The relationship between China and India, as major developing economies and voices of the Global South, influences global dynamics. BRICS provides a platform for dialogue, advancing common interests, and managing differences.

item.title: Xi Jinping attends BRICS summit in New Delhi, discusses global development
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping participated in the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi. He delivered a speech on "BRICS: A Responsible Vanguard in Global Development," highlighting 20 years of cooperation and the bloc's influence on emerging markets and developing countries. Xi emphasized BRICS' role in overcoming global challenges and supporting the Global South.

item.title: India's First Investment Project in Kyrgyzstan, Avelum Partner, Reaches Production Stage
item.description: The Solton-Sary gold recovery plant, India's first investment project in Kyrgyzstan from exploration to production, has launched in test mode. Avelum Partner LLC, a subsidiary of India's Deccan Gold Mines Ltd, partnered with Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC.

item.title: India's first investment project in Kyrgyzstan, Avelum Partner, reaches production stage
item.description: The Solton-Sary gold recovery plant has begun test operations, marking a significant milestone for Kyrgyzstan's 35th independence anniversary. Avelum Partner LLC, an Indian subsidiary of Deccan Gold Mines Ltd, partnered with Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC, represents India's first full-cycle investment project in Kyrgyzstan, from exploration to industrial production, with $34.2 million invested.

item.title: Somoniyon School Operates Without a License After Expiration
item.description: The Somoniyon school is currently operating without a license, as its activity permit expired on October 17, 2024. The head of the Education and Science Oversight Agency stated that the Afghan government's changes... (incomplete source text)

item.title: Nearly 100,000 Uzbek Citizens Returned from Russia in 10 Days
item.description: Almost 100,000 Uzbek citizens returned to Uzbekistan from Russia between August 25 and September 5, according to the Migration Agency of Uzbekistan. Of these, 54,885 arrived directly, and 41,530 came via Kazakhstan. Assistance was provided to 5,467 individuals.

item.title: Nearly 100,000 Uzbek citizens returned from Russia in 10 days
item.description: According to Uzbekistan's Migration Agency, approximately 96,415 Uzbek citizens returned from Russia between August 25 and September 5. Of these, 54,885 arrived directly, while 41,530 entered via Kazakhstan. The agency provided practical assistance to 5,467 individuals and is processing 6,413 appeals. Over 2,500 job openings were identified through negotiations with employers.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev begins state visit to South Korea
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and his wife have arrived in Seoul for a state visit. The agenda includes negotiations with President Lee Jae-myung, meetings with officials and business leaders, and participation in the Central Asia-South Korea summit.

item.title: Tajikistan's economy: A look back at 35 years of development since the 1990s crisis
item.description: This report examines the economic path of Tajikistan over the past 35 years, tracing its development from the crisis of the 1990s to its current economy with a GDP of hundreds of billions of somoni. Further details are available.
